chief_complaint: facial swelling, distended neck veins, and shortness of breath when bending over
hpi_details: 63M heavy smoker presenting with facial plethora, upper extremity edema, positive Pemberton sign, and right upper lobe lung mass compressing the SVC.
ideas: He thinks his high blood pressure is backing up blood into his head or that a severe sinus blockage is trapping fluid in his face.
concerns: He is worried that his decades of heavy smoking have caught up with him and that he has developed inoperable lung cancer.
expectations: He hopes to get a chest CT scan today to find out what is pressing on his neck and medication to relieve the choking sensation.
social_hx: Heavy smoker (40 pack-year history), social drinker, employed full-time

available_results.value: Right upper-lobe and mediastinal mass causing severe superior vena cava narrowing with extensive venous collaterals

clinical_knowledge.topic: Superior Vena Cava (SVC) Syndrome evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Superior Vena Cava (SVC) Syndrome is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic protocol for Superior Vena Cava SVC Syndrome, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Superior Vena Cava (SVC) Syndrome.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Heart failure without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Stridor or severe breathlessness — airway compromise needs urgent evaluation.

Refer to specialty team and provide comprehensive patient counseling

Implement targeted therapeutic interventions per evidence-based clinical practice guidelines.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

teaching.one_liner: A lung mass compresses the superior vena cava, obstructing venous return from the head and arms and causing facial swelling, distended neck veins, and breathlessness when bending forward.
differentials: Superior mediastinal lymphadenopathy from another cause
red_flags: Stridor or severe breathlessness — airway compromise needs urgent evaluation

must_ask.say: Has your face or arms been swelling, especially in the morning?
Does the swelling or breathlessness get worse when you bend over or lie flat?
How long have you smoked, and how much?
Have you noticed the veins in your neck or chest becoming more prominent?
Any unexplained weight loss or a new cough?

history.answer: Doctor, my face has been swelling up and I've been feeling short of breath, especially whenever I bend over.
The swelling is mainly in my face, neck, and both of my arms, but my legs and belly look completely normal.
It started gradually about three weeks ago and has been steadily getting worse each week.
It's worst when I first wake up in the morning, but my face stays puffy and congested throughout the entire day.
My shirt collars feel very tight and my rings are stuck on my fingers, but when I push on my arms it doesn't leave a deep dent like dough.
Whenever I bend down to tie my shoes or lie flat on my back, my head feels full of intense pressure and it gets much harder to breathe.
Yes, I noticed prominent blue veins bulging and branching out across my neck and the top of my chest.
I've had a nagging dry cough for about a month, but I haven't coughed up any blood or phlegm.
I actually haven't gained fluid weight, but I've unintentionally lost about five pounds over the past month.
I get winded when bending over or moving around, but I don't wake up gasping for air in the middle of the night.
No, neither of my legs is swollen, red, hot, or painful at all.
My urine is a clear light yellow. There is no foam, no dark brown color, and the amount hasn't decreased.
My stomach hasn't gotten bigger, my eyes and skin are not yellow, and I haven't noticed easy bruising or bleeding.
No, I haven't had a sore throat, skin boils, fever, or any recent infections.
No, I'm not unusually sensitive to the cold, I don't have dry skin, and my bowel movements are regular.
My appetite has been a bit lower than usual lately, but I eat balanced meals and don't have diarrhea.
I haven't had any recent surgeries, I haven't taken long flights, and I haven't been bedridden or immobilized.
I don't take amlodipine, steroids, or regular anti-inflammatory painkillers.
I don't eat unusually salty food, and my job doesn't require standing for long hours.
I've had high blood pressure for five years, but my doctor checked my heart and kidneys recently and said they were working well.
My voice sounds a little hoarser than usual lately, but I haven't had any noisy breathing, wheezing, or trouble swallowing.
I thought maybe my blood pressure spiked or a bad sinus blockage was making all the blood rush straight to my head.
I've smoked two packs a day for forty years, and I'm terrified this means I have a lung tumor that has spread too far to treat.
I want to get a chest scan right away to see what is choking off my neck veins and get something to ease this pressure.
I have high blood pressure and mild high cholesterol, both diagnosed about five years ago.
I had an appendectomy in my twenties, but no other operations or hospital stays.
I take lisinopril 10 milligrams once every morning for my blood pressure, and no over-the-counter supplements.
I have no known allergies to medications, foods, or iodine contrast dyes.
I have smoked about one pack of cigarettes a day for 40 years.
I drink one or two beers socially on the weekend, but nothing heavy.
I work full-time at an office desk job and live with my wife in an apartment.
My father passed away from a heart attack in his seventies, and my mother had diabetes, but there is no family history of cancer.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 135/85 mmHg, pulse 78 beats per minute, respiratory rate 18 breaths per minute, body temperature 36.7°C, and oxygen saturation 96% on room air.
Marked facial plethora, periorbital edema, and cyanotic congestion of the face and neck with visible superficial venules.
Prominent periorbital puffiness and bilateral conjunctival suffusion without scleral icterus or proptosis.
No cervical, supraclavicular, or axillary lymphadenopathy palpable.
Thyroid gland is normal in size, non-tender, without palpable nodules or bruits.
Jugular veins are markedly engorged and distended bilaterally up to the mandibular angle without normal venous pulsations.
Dilated tortuous collateral veins visible over the anterior chest wall; positive Pemberton sign with rapid facial flushing and dyspnea when raising both arms.
Decreased breath sounds over the right upper lung field; no stridor, wheezes, or bibasilar crackles.
Normal S1 and S2 with regular rate and rhythm; no S3 gallop, S4, pericardial friction rub, or murmurs heard.
Abdomen is flat and symmetric without caput medusae, dilated veins, or distension.
Liver and spleen are not palpable below the costal margins without hepatosplenomegaly or tenderness.
No shifting dullness or fluid wave elicited.
Mild non-pitting edema of both upper extremities and hands; no pretibial pitting edema in either lower extremity.
Calves are symmetric in circumference with no localized tenderness, warmth, erythema, or palpable cords.
